feature: Compression engine `headroom` (OmniRoute's own SmartCrusher: tabular JSON compaction via GCF/TOON), plus the external Headroom proxy integration (/api/headroom/status|start|stop, settings.headroomUrl, HEADROOM_URL, HEADROOM_PYTHON)
what_it_does:
The two "headroom" features are unrelated to each other (maintainer comment on #12306).

1) Built-in engine. It is OmniRoute-internal; only the gcf/ codec is vendored, from gcf-typescript@00972f2d. It runs only when a compression plan includes it. It scans non-system, non-developer message text: whole-string JSON arrays, ```json fences and Responses tool outputs mapped to role:tool. It replaces any JSON array of at least minRows objects with a ```gcf-generic or ```toon block when that block is shorter in characters. The provider receives the compact block with no legend; reconstructHeadroom is only a test oracle.

2) External integration, which only manages and reports on a separate process. status runs `which headroom` on an augmented PATH, looks for python >=3.10 and GETs {url}/health with a 1.5 s timeout. start (loopback URL only) spawns `headroom proxy --port N` with the inherited environment and no flags. stop sends SIGTERM to the recorded PID. No request path forwards traffic to headroomUrl.
defaults:
- Compression master switch: enabled=false, defaultMode=off.
- Engine config default is enabled=true (per step). The engines map is display-only (enginesExplicit=false) until an engines row is saved.
- minRows=8; accepted range 2..10000.
- The engine is not in the seeded default combo [session-dedup, lite].
- Engine catalog: lossy=false, cacheImpact=low, isSingleMode=false.
- External URL: settings.headroomUrl, else the HEADROOM_URL env var, else http://localhost:8787. HEADROOM_PYTHON is optional. There is no auto-start.
controls:
- /api/settings/compression: enabled, defaultMode, engines.headroom.enabled, headroom.minRows, exclusions[], activeComboId, stackedPipeline.
- Compression combos: /api/context/combos, plus /[id]/assignments to attach one to a routing combo.
- Request header `x-omniroute-compression`: values `engine:headroom`, `<combo name or id>`, `off`, `default`, `allow-lossy`. It is honoured only when the master switch is on; `engine:headroom` also needs engines.headroom.enabled.
- Routing-combo compressionMode / compressionOverride.
- Per-API-key compressionEnabled=false (opt-out only; the gateway is keyless).
- External: settings.headroomUrl, env HEADROOM_URL and HEADROOM_PYTHON, and the PATH of omniroute.service.
- POST /api/headroom/start and /stop (LOCAL_ONLY tier).
- Dashboard: /dashboard/context/headroom (engine page) and the Headroom card in Settings > Advanced (proxy).
applies_to:
- CX: unreachable today. The codex/* exclusion matches provider codex, and the master switch is off. If it were reachable, JSON arrays inside Responses function_call_output / local_shell outputs would be rewritten (the developer turn is skipped).
- FW: calls to cx/gpt-6-* also resolve to provider codex, so the same exclusion applies (all 1600 live requests were skipped as 'excluded'). Chat messages and tool results would be scanned. Making it reachable means removing codex/* for every lane, and with the master switch on that also turns on reactive/last-resort history compaction for FW, because FW is not native passthrough.
- SEARCH: N/A. The /v1/search and local /v1/alpha/search route files contain no compression or chatCore references (rg).
- External proxy: no consumer. OmniRoute never routes requests to headroomUrl.
quality_risk:
1) Not lossless at the value level. tryCompactJson parses with JSON.parse into JavaScript doubles, so integers above 2^53 are rounded.
   - Local probe: ids 1234567890123456710 and ...711 were both restored as 1234567890123456800, and the literal 1.50 became 1.5.
   - Upstream round-trip tests compare against the already-parsed object, so they cannot catch this.
2) The model sees a different format with no legend: GCF (`|` separators, `~` for missing, `meta>score` nested paths) or TOON. Upstream has no model-comprehension eval. Its benchmark json fixture is a single object, so headroom's budget baseline (json=160) equals the engines that do nothing.
3) The Codex protected-tool eligibility guard is ignored (only the codex-responses engine reads it). Probe: a `read` tool output was compacted, so apply_patch context or fixtures copied from it can mismatch. Precedent: #7102, where compacting an array in the developer turn broke Codex plan mode.
4) Upstream's own opt-in fidelity gate rejects headroom output. Probe: the 20-row case failed 'numeric' and the big-int case failed 'protected-tokens'.
5) A proxy started from OmniRoute would run Headroom defaults (per 0.39.0 help text): Kompress ML compression on, semantic cache on, rate limit 60 rpm / 100000 tpm, and the default OpenAI upstream. Headroom upstream has open fidelity bugs #3544, #3098 and #3545.
cache_effect:
- The engine is deterministic: the probe gave identical output on repeat, and ties go to GCF for cache stability. It skips system/developer messages.
- Applied from turn 1, the prefix stays stable.
- Turning it on or off mid-session rewrites every earlier message that holds a compactable array, which breaks the cached prefix. CX is 94% cached over 24h (91,426,944 of 97,094,617 input tokens).
- The cache-aware guard does not stop it on caching providers; only aggressive and ultra are downgraded.
- Making it reachable also enables reactive compaction for large FW contexts, which rewrites history and breaks the cache.
- An external proxy would add a second transformer in front of OmniRoute's cache affinity.
token_effect:
- Request side only; output (~1% of tokens) is untouched.
- Live: nothing saved. Snapshot analytics show totalRequests 0, totalSkipped 1600 (all 'excluded'), totalTokensSaved 0. There is no live data on how much input is compactable.
- Local synthetic probe, counted with o200k_base as a stand-in for the GPT-6 tokenizer:

| Input | Characters | Tokens |
|---|---|---|
| 20-row compact array | 2387 -> 1564 (-34.5%) | 922 -> 830 (-10.0%) |
| Same rows pretty-printed in a fence | 3645 -> 1589 | 1455 -> 839 (-42.3%, mostly whitespace) |
| 7 rows | unchanged | unchanged |

- The size gate counts characters, not tokens. Upstream's ">=30%" test figure is also a character metric on a 20-row array.
- Savings only reach uncached input.

1. A lane's sanitized replay shows compactable arrays are a material share of its uncached input.

feature: Compression engine "lite": whitespace/format cleanup, system-prompt dedup, tool-result truncation (compressToolResults/maxToolLength), redundant-message removal, image placeholder
what_it_does:
Source read at the pin. Five rewrites run in order on messages[]. Responses input[] is first adapted to messages. (1) Whitespace: strips trailing [ 	] from each line and collapses 
{3,} to 

 in every string-content message, including tool outputs and user text. It skips role "system" only when preserveSystemPrompt is true, and it has no toggle (lite.ts L50-81, L251). (2) System-dedup: drops a later system message whose first 200 trimmed chars match an earlier one; it is off when preserveSystemPrompt is true (L83-105). (3) Tool-compress: truncates every role:"tool" string longer than the cap (default 2000) at a word boundary and appends "
...[truncated]"; controlled by lite.compressToolResults (L148-169, L259-263). (4) Redundant-remove: drops a message whose role and string content equal the previous message; role tool has been exempt since #13429; tool_calls are ignored and there is no toggle (L171-201, L265). (5) Image placeholder: replaces data:image image_url parts with "[image: fmt]" only when supportsVision===false (L203-241). CODEX GUARD: none. bodyAdapter.ts L120-145 maps function_call_output, custom_tool_call_output, local_shell_call_output and apply_patch_call_output to role:"tool" (L137). The protected-tool/eligibility metadata (L144, L154-203) is read only by the codex-responses engine (engines/codexResponses/index.ts L251, L279-281). pipelineGuards.ts only reverts a result that grew in size; stackedStepCore.ts is opt-in bail-out plus telemetry; the fidelity gate is opt-in and stacked-only. isDocumentLikeRead exists only in RTK (engines/rtk/index.ts L250-253). Observed in my probe with the live lite config: exec_command output 6980→2013 chars, protected "read" output 6980→2013, apply_patch custom output 7820→2249, all truncated. LOSSLESS SUBSET: none of the five steps is byte-lossless, and no config keeps only lossless ones. The nearest config (compressToolResults=false, preserveSystemPrompt=true) still rewrote tool output 6980→6380 chars and turned a diff context line " " into "".
defaults: types.ts L421-441: enabled=false, defaultMode="off", autoTriggerMode="lite", autoTriggerTokens=0, preserveSystemPrompt=true, preserveSystemPromptMode="always", lite={compressToolResults:true}. The engines map defaults to all disabled (L430 area). The cap resolves as lite.maxToolLength, then env OMNIROUTE_LITE_MAX_TOOL_LENGTH, then 2000; valid range 256-1,000,000 (lite.ts L24-48; ENVIRONMENT.md L576). The cavemanAdapter.ts L217-242 schema also defaults compressToolResults=true and maxToolLength=2000. Since PR #14529, SAFE_DEFAULT_PIPELINE is [session-dedup, lite] (lossyRequestPolicy.ts L19).
controls: Settings API /api/settings/compression: keys enabled (master switch), defaultMode, exclusions, lite.compressToolResults, lite.maxToolLength (null clears it; src/lib/db/compression.ts L535-566), preserveSystemPrompt / preserveSystemPromptMode, engines.lite.enabled (the header engine:lite requires it), autoTriggerMode / autoTriggerTokens, activeComboId, comboOverrides, contextBudget.mode. Compression combos (pipeline steps with per-step config such as {engine:"lite", config:{compressToolResults:false}}; step config wins, cavemanAdapter.ts L280-297). Request header x-omniroute-compression: off | default | safe | allow-lossy | engine:<id> | <combo name or id> (chatCore/headers.ts L41-44; planResolution.ts L32-58). A header cannot enable compression while the master is off (strategySelector.ts L126-136). Routing-combo config.compressionMode or compressionOverride="lite" (chatCore.ts L1573-1597). Per-API-key compressionEnabled can only opt out (chatCore.ts L1446), and the gateway is keyless. Env OMNIROUTE_LITE_MAX_TOOL_LENGTH.
applies_to: CX: blocked by exclusions ["codex/*"]. The snapshot shows 1600 of 1600 compression skips with reason "excluded". An excluded target is byte-identical, and the exclusion also forces config.enabled=false (chatCore.ts L1439-1449, L1496-1498). If unblocked, steps (1) and (3) would rewrite or truncate Codex tool outputs, including protected read/grep outputs and apply_patch custom outputs, so OFF. FW (/v1/chat/completions: S3 memory lane, sweep, runtimes): lite is reachable only with master enabled=true. Step (1) changes user document text and tool text (quote/provenance fidelity). Step (3) truncates tool results. Step (4) drops a consecutive assistant message with identical ""/text content but different tool_calls, leaving an orphan tool_call_id (upstream 400); content:null is safe. Other body fields (response_format, tools) are preserved. Step (5) is a no-op because GPT-6 codex models have supportsVision:true (shared.ts L338-347). SEARCH: N/A. rg finds no chatCore/compress reference in src/app/api/v1/search or src/app/api/v1/alpha/search.
quality_risk: High for GPT-6 max-effort workers. Truncation at 2000 chars keeps only 0.8-20.7% of the tokens of real large outputs (chatCore.ts 0.8%, snapshot JSON 2.4%, token-practice.md 6.1%, lite.ts 20.7%). Issue #13178 reports a 12.1 KB result cut to about 1.9K chars. Whitespace step: in real files it changed 55 lone-space diff context lines in one git show and collapsed 10 PEP8 double-blank runs in validate.py. That can break exact-match edits and patches, and quote matching in memory extraction. Redundant-remove can orphan tool calls (probe2, observed). Upstream mislabels lite: engineCatalog.ts L58-70 says lossy:false, "zero semantic change… Always safe to leave on", cacheImpact "none". lossyRequestPolicy.ts L19/L49-71 substitutes session-dedup+lite for downgraded lossy plans, and the live "Standard Savings" combo is described as "Default lossless dedup and whitespace compression". A downgraded "safe" plan therefore truncates tool results. The chatCore.ts L1431-1438 comment claims native Codex compresses "with codex tool-output eligibility guards", which is false for lite.
cache_effect: Lite is not prefix-neutral because it rewrites message bytes. It is deterministic and causal, so it is prefix-stable once applied consistently: the probe confirmed that lite applied to N messages equals the first N messages of lite applied to N+1. Cost: one cache miss from the first rewritten item onward each time lite is switched on mid-session or applied intermittently (header on some calls only, autoTriggerTokens threshold crossing, cap or env change). The system prompt stays untouched under preserveSystemPromptMode "always" (cacheAwareConfig.ts L44-60). Against the measured 24h cache of 91,426,944 cached out of 97,094,617 input (~94%), any toggle turns cached tokens into uncached tokens for that request.
proposed_config: No live change; the current state already matches this resolution and keeps the default path byte-identical. Keep enabled=false, defaultMode="off", exclusions=["codex/*"], autoTriggerTokens=0, preserveSystemPromptMode="always", activeComboId=null, comboOverrides={}. Set no routing-combo compressionMode or compressionOverride="lite", and have lanes send no x-omniroute-compression header (or send "off"). Optional hardening, with no traffic effect while enabled=false: PUT /api/settings/compression {"lite":{"compressToolResults":false}}, leave maxToolLength unset, then GET read-back. This stops the SAFE_DEFAULT_PIPELINE and Standard Savings fallback from truncating tool results if the master switch is ever enabled for another engine. It does not cover aggressive's internal lite pass (aggressive.ts L190-194). Do not save the engines map: that sets enginesExplicit and changes the derived default. A lossless-only lite config cannot be reached, because whitespace and redundant-remove run whenever lite runs. Making lite opt-in for a lane would require removing its provider from exclusions and setting enabled=true. That also turns on reactive and last-resort compaction for all non-native-Codex traffic (chatCore.ts L1449, L2139, L2213), which breaks the byte-identical default rule.
overturn_condition: Revisit only when all of these hold. (a) Upstream lite honors Codex eligibility or a per-tool allowlist (the #13178 follow-up), and whitespace and redundant-remove get toggles or redundant-remove checks tool_calls. (b) Lite becomes reachable per lane without the master switch or reactive compaction (lane- or key-scoped enablement, or a separate reactive-compaction switch). (c) The lane's own A/B at its production model and effort shows quality at least at parity (task success, JSON-schema validity, tool-call 400 rate, edit-apply success) and provider-counted input savings larger than the one-time cache miss. The current measurement is 0.00-0.18% o200k savings for the whitespace step.

feature: Compression lane selector: how one lane opts in while the default path stays unchanged (options: x-omniroute-compression header, routing-combo override, per-key opt-out, exclusions, second instance)
what_it_does:
ORDER (chatCore.ts; the file is identical at a58000c7 and dd6e9607e): 1) L1399-1402: builds a read-only view of Responses input[] as messages to estimate tokens. It is a new object and the body is never assigned from it. 2) L1427: reads the master `enabled` flag. 3) L1439-1442: isCompressionExcluded({provider, effectiveModel}). 4) L1446: per-key opt-out; a keyless request has apiKeyInfo=null, so compression stays on. 5) L1447-1449: prompt compression = master AND not excluded AND key on; reactive compaction = master AND not excluded (the header and the key never affect it). 6) L1496-1498: an excluded target or key opt-out sets config.enabled=false. 7) L1562-1619: a routing combo applies its compressionMode through comboOverrides, or its assigned compression combo as a stacked pipeline. 8) L1639: header lookup, then resolveBasePlan in this order: master off gives off and the header cannot enable it; then a recognized header; routing override; activeComboId; auto-trigger (only if tokens>0); derived default (the engines map if enginesExplicit, otherwise the legacy defaultMode). Lossy steps are replaced by session-dedup+lite unless the header is allow-lossy, engine:<id> or a combo name. Then adaptive budgeting and the cache-aware rule (codex: aggressive/ultra become standard). 9) L1655-1688: legacy default-combo fallback when the plan is stacked. 10) L1693: output styles run if enabled and header is not off. 11) L1787 and L1913: engines run only when mode is not off, and the body is replaced only when compressed. 12) L2138-2162: proactive compaction when reactive AND not nativeCodexPassthrough AND estimate > floor((limit-tools)*0.7), with an adapter restore round-trip. 13) L2212-2231: last-resort compaction at or above the limit, same gates. 14) L2250-2277: the 400 budget gate.
ANSWERS: (a) Header off on CX passthrough: the compression code does not change the body. No round-trip happens: step 1 is only a view, and steps 12-13 skip passthrough. Under the live config the header is irrelevant because codex/* forces off. (b) Header off on chat/completions: prompt compression is skipped, but steps 12-13 still run above the threshold whenever master is on and the target is not excluded. (c) codex/* does match combo targets, because chatCore runs per concrete target with provider=codex and an alias-resolved model. The matcher checks only the bare model and the provider/model composite. It does not check the endpoint, the combo name or the client alias, so cx/* never matches. (d) Codex 0.157.1 supports http_headers and env_http_headers per provider. (e) The OpenAI SDKs accept default_headers (Python) and defaultHeaders (Node). (f) A combo name works only for safe engines, needs the same master and exclusion gates, and CX would have to send a non-catalog model slug. Not recommended. (g) A second DATA_DIR instance is not needed; see overturn_condition. ONE MECHANISM: the x-omniroute-compression request header, whose value names a per-lane compression combo.

With no exclusions setting, exclusions=[]. Proactive compaction ratio is 0.7 (range 0.1-0.99), stored in the DB at key_value compression/proactiveConfig; no API route writes it. With no header, the operator plan applies. Per-key compressionEnabled defaults to true.

The response echoes X-OmniRoute-Compression: <mode>; source=<src>. The base executor does not forward client headers upstream (base.ts L504). CLIENTS: Codex [model_providers.<id>] http_headers (static) and env_http_headers (header name to env var; the header is omitted when the variable is unset or blank). openai-python default_headers and per-call extra_headers; openai-node defaultHeaders.
applies_to: CX: yes. /v1/responses to codex is native passthrough (passthroughHelpers L47-67), so steps 12-13 never run and the default path stays byte-identical at any size. The header is carried by Codex env_http_headers. FW: yes. chat/completions is translated, not passthrough; the header is carried by SDK default_headers. After the master flip the default path is byte-identical only below the proactive threshold. SEARCH: N/A. The /v1/alpha/search (local) and /v1/search routes contain no compression code (0 matches); a provider-level header reaches them and is ignored.
quality_risk: Default CX: none, per source reading. Default FW after the flip: reactive or last-resort compaction trims history above floor(0.7*(limit-tools)), about 610k estimated tokens at the registry limit of 872000. Today those requests pass untouched below the limit or fail with 400 at or above it. Neither header off nor the per-key opt-out can stop this (#11255). Opt-in lanes: 1) the 'safe' pipeline is not lossless. lite truncates tool messages over 2000 chars to '...[truncated]' (lite.ts L24, L148-169, L259-260) even though the catalog marks lite lossy:false. Codex shell and apply_patch outputs are eligible. 2) A routing-combo selection without a lossy header is silently downgraded to session-dedup+lite. 3) Static reading, not executed: with the live builtin stackedPipeline and the isDefault combo default-caveman, a header naming a stacked combo, or engine:session-dedup, triggers the L1655-1688 fallback. That sets compressionComboApplied, so L1775-1785 never copies the header's pipeline, and default-caveman [session-dedup, lite] runs while the response header still reports source=request-header.
cache_effect: The selector itself has no cache effect on the default path: CX bytes are unchanged, and FW is unchanged below the threshold. For an opt-in lane, codex is a caching provider, so the system prompt is preserved and aggressive/ultra become standard (cachingAware L112-126). Any rewrite of input items still changes the cached prefix from the first changed item onward. Measured prompt-cache share (coordinator): 91,426,944 cached of 97,094,617 input, about 94.2%. Snapshot cache-health (24h): 1,443 warm and 43 uncached of 1,486 calls, cacheReadTotal 110,864,768. So an engine that changes the prefix from turn to turn can cost more than it saves.
token_effect: Default path: 0. Snapshot totalTokensSaved=0 with 1600 skips, all 'excluded'. After the flip those 'excluded' skip rows stop being written; that is a telemetry-only change. Opt-in bounds from the measured split: output is 117,065 of about 9.54M call-log tokens (about 1.2%), which caps any output-style saving. Input compression mainly reaches the roughly 6% uncached input unless the prefix stays stable across turns.

feature: Compression engine: CCR (Content-Compression-Retrieve, content-addressed retrieve markers)
what_it_does: A stackable engine (priority 4) that runs before translation. It looks at every non-system message except role:tool and user turns made only of tool_result. Any string content or text part of at least minChars is replaced whole by its first 200 chars + "… [CCR retrieve hash=<sha256[:24]> chars=N]", but only when that is shorter. The original goes to a principal-scoped in-process LRU (5,000 entries, 64 MiB global, 16 MiB per principal, 2 MiB per block, 24h TTL) backed by a SQLite durable tier. The engine runs only when the request's tools[] advertises omniroute_ccr_retrieve, either exactly or namespaced with __ . / :. On at least one replacement it prepends a 743-char "[CCR protocol]" system message. Nothing is rehydrated on the request path: the model has to call the MCP tool omniroute_ccr_retrieve through a client MCP link (full read capped at 256 KiB; also head/tail/lines/grep/stats). Operators can POST /api/compression/retrieve (anon bucket only). H8 feedback raises the effective minChars after each retrieval; after 3 retrievals that block is never compressed.
defaults: Engine: minChars 600 (UI range 100-1,000,000; the validator accepts >=1), retrievalRampFactor 2, retrieval threshold 3, preamble 200 chars, TTL 24h (60s-7d), durable store on for blocks <=512 KB, MCP full-read cap 256 KiB. Compression settings: enabled=false, defaultMode=off, autoTriggerTokens=0 (at this pin 0 means never; the check is >0). The ccr detail block is {minChars:600, retrievalRampFactor:2}. engines.ccr is off in the backfilled display map.
controls:
PUT /api/settings/compression:
- enabled: master switch and hard kill; a header cannot re-enable it.
- exclusions: codex/* bypasses the whole pipeline byte-identically.
- engines.ccr.enabled: needed only for the header value engine:ccr. Storing any engines row sets enginesExplicit=true, which makes the whole engines map the default plan.
- ccr.minChars and ccr.retrievalRampFactor.
- stackedPipeline, defaultMode, autoTrigger*, activeComboId, comboOverrides and compressionComboId also steer the plan.

Compression combos: pipeline {engine:"ccr"}, which can be assigned to a routing combo.

Header x-omniroute-compression: off | default | engine:ccr | <combo name or id>.

Client side: the lane's tools[] must carry omniroute_ccr_retrieve from the OmniRoute MCP (settings mcpEnabled and mcpTransport stdio|sse|streamable-http; client runs omniroute --mcp), with a matching principal (API-key id or __anon__). The "sticky-on" label is description text only. Any unfiltered OmniRoute MCP connection therefore advertises the tool; MCP_TOOL_DENY / MCP_TOOL_ALLOW can drop it.

Env: COMPRESSION_CCR_RETRIEVAL_RAMP_FACTOR, COMPRESSION_CCR_DURABLE_STORE.

Per-key opt-out: apiKey.compressionEnabled=false.
applies_to:
CX: blocked three ways. The codex/* exclusion forces enabled=false before the plan is resolved, the master switch is off, and Codex's tools[] has no omniroute_ccr_retrieve (mcpEnabled=false). If CCR were forced on, the Responses adapter would make user, developer and assistant input items candidates and drop the protocol note on restore.

FW: no. cognee and Hindsight advertise their own function tools and json_schema and cannot run an MCP retrieve loop, so the engine skips itself. Their GPT-6 targets also resolve to provider codex and hit codex/*.

SEARCH: N/A. The /v1/alpha/search and /v1/search routes never call the compression pipeline.
cache_effect:
The upstream catalog documents cacheImpact "low". The source shows these prefix breaks:
1. Chat format: the first request with a replacement prepends a 743-char system message at index 0, which invalidates the whole cached prefix. The message disappears again when replacements drop to 0.
2. The inflation guard reverts turns that do not shrink (a single block under about 1,000 chars loses to the 743-char note), so CCR switches on and off between turns.
3. H8 ramp: after 1 retrieval, blocks shorter than 2x minChars go back to plain text; after 3 retrievals the block is never compressed. Either change rewrites earlier history.
4. When the store rejects a block for budget, the text goes back in.
5. Keyless mode shares __anon__ retrieval counters, so one lane's retrievals can rewrite another lane's prompt, but only where the two carry byte-identical blocks.

Steady state is deterministic (sha256 plus a fixed preamble). Each break turns cached input into uncached input, which works against Codex sticky cache continuity (about 94% of input cached).
proposed_config:
No write is needed; the live state already matches. Keep these values, written so they merge with other feature resolutions:
- /api/settings/compression: enabled=false, defaultMode=off, exclusions=["codex/*"].
- Any stored engines row keeps ccr.enabled=false.
- No compression combo pipeline contains {engine:"ccr"}; activeComboId=null.
- Leave ccr.minChars=600 and retrievalRampFactor=2 as they are (inert).
- /api/settings: mcpEnabled=false.
- No lane sends x-omniroute-compression: engine:ccr or a ccr combo.

The durable-store env value (COMPRESSION_CCR_DURABLE_STORE) belongs to the ionizer and session-dedup-fuzzy resolutions, which are its writers. Changing it would need a restart, which is out of scope here.
overturn_condition:
Reopen only if one of these holds:
- (a) A lane whose client advertises omniroute_ccr_retrieve over a working MCP link with a matching principal, and whose input is mostly long, uncached, non-tool text. A same-prompt A/B must then show no quality loss and lower total usage, counting retrieval turns and cache misses.
- (b) Upstream adds request-path rehydration, or makes the protocol note and H8 flips prefix-safe.

Only then, reach it this way:
1. Assign a [{engine:"ccr"}] compression combo to a routing combo used only by that lane. This is the one path that leaves the default route alone. The source shows a header-selected combo is overridden by the seeded default combo while stackedPipeline is the builtin rtk+caveman.
2. Do not use engine:ccr. It needs a stored engines row, and that row turns the whole engines map into the global default.
3. Turn the master switch on only after its side effects (for example reactive compaction) are dealt with.
4. For GPT-6 lanes, remove or narrow codex/*, since CX and FW both resolve to provider codex. Use mcpEnabled=true and client MCP_TOOL_ALLOW=omniroute_ccr_retrieve.

feature: Compression engine session-dedup: cross-turn block dedup, plus an optional fuzzy near-duplicate pass
what_it_does: A messages-only stacked engine (stackPriority 3). On a request with several messages, pass 1 hashes every line-aligned suffix block of each non-system text; a block must be at least minBlockChars characters and 3 lines. Pass 2 finds, in each later message, the longest block whose first owner is an earlier message. It replaces that one block with `[dedup:ref sha=<24hex>]` and replaces nothing else in the message. The first occurrence is always kept. The hash is a SHA-256 prefix, and an equality check guards against collisions. Only shared message tails can match. A request with a single text gets intra-message dedup instead. The optional fuzzy pass (live: off) replaces a whole string message that is at least 85% Jaccard-similar to an earlier one with a CCR store marker. Nothing is reconstructed: markers reach the model as they are.
defaults:
- **Engine:** minBlockChars 80 (schema range 1..100000). MIN_BLOCK_LINES is fixed at 3. fuzzy is false (minJaccard 0.85, shingleSize 3, MAX_FUZZY_BLOCKS 200). Per-message caps are 2000 suffix starts and 8 MiB. The engine schema default is enabled.
- **Master switch:** compression enabled=false and defaultMode off.
- **When the master is on:** requests without the header are downgraded to SAFE_DEFAULT_PIPELINE [session-dedup, lite]. The seeded 'Standard Savings' combo is also [session-dedup, lite] (#14529).

- **Settings:** GET/PUT /api/settings/compression, or the dashboard page /dashboard/context/session-dedup. - **Combos:** compression combos at /api/context/combos, which can be assigned to a routing combo. A per-step config inside a pipeline overrides the sessionDedup detail.
- **Header:** x-omniroute-compression accepts off, default, safe, allow-lossy, engine:<id> or <combo>. It cannot turn compression on while the master is off.

cache_effect:
- **Append-only history keeps the prefix stable (derived from source, not executed).** Pass 2 reads only earlier messages; SHA-256 and the per-message caps are deterministic. The engine is not worker-eligible (runs in-process) and not memoized. So turn N+1 reproduces turn N's rewrites and the cached prefix holds.
- **Exception 1:** intra-message dedup runs only when exactly one text exists. On the next turn the first text item changes, which costs one cache miss from that item onward.
- **Exception 2:** fuzzy depends on the CCR store. Past 200 blocks it returns nothing, so every earlier fuzzy replacement reverts at once.
- **Cache-aware layer:** adds no protection; deterministicOnly has no consumer.
- **Reaching the engine changes the default path.** It needs enabled=true and removing codex/*. That also turns on proactive and last-resort reactive compaction for non-passthrough FW traffic above the threshold (default ratio 0.7), which rewrites the default path.

feature: Compression engine: RTK (OmniRoute's command-output filters)
what_it_does:
OmniRoute's own TypeScript RTK engine, separate from the rtk-ai binary. It rewrites tool-result text in the request before it goes upstream, in five steps per tool message:
1. Detects the command from the tool call's command, else from a command prefix in the first 4 lines, else from broad content regexes.
2. Picks one filter: 55 builtin JSON filters, plus $DATA_DIR/rtk and trusted project .rtk filters (RTK TOML v1 or JSON). generic-output is the fallback. Filters strip, keep, collapse and head/tail-truncate.
3. Collapses 3 or more identical consecutive lines (engine-wide dedup).
4. Applies a hard cap of 120 lines × 1.5 (minimal) / × 1 / × 0.5 and 12000 chars. It keeps head/tail 24 lines (16 at aggressive) plus priority lines matching /error|failed|exception|traceback|TS\d{4}|FAIL|✖/i, and inserts [rtk:truncated N lines] markers.
5. Skips filters and the cap for "document-like" text (unknown type, no command, no Error:/Exception:/Traceback).

Shape handling:
- **Chat:** role:"tool" messages and Anthropic tool_result blocks (blocks carrying cache_control are left untouched). Tool names are known, so non-shell tools skip filters and dedup but not the cap.
- **Responses:** function_call_output, custom_tool_call_output, local_shell_call_output and apply_patch_call_output become role:"tool" messages with no tool name.
- **Optional features, all off live:** code-block stripping, renderers, grouping, raw-output retention.
defaults:
Upstream code (types.ts L421-443, L469-491):
- Compression: enabled=false, defaultMode "off", every engine off, stackedPipeline [rtk standard, caveman full].
- rtkConfig: enabled=false, intensity "minimal", applyToToolResults=true, applyToCodeBlocks and applyToAssistantMessages false, maxLinesPerResult 120, maxCharsPerResult 12000, deduplicateThreshold 3, customFiltersEnabled=true, trustProjectFilters=false, rawOutputRetention "never" (1 MiB / 100000 files / 30 d), grouping, renderers and stripCodeComments off.
- Upstream catalog: lossy=true, cacheImpact "moderate". A request that did not ask for rtk is downgraded to session-dedup+lite.

The upstream doc RTK_COMPRESSION.md (v3.8.40, 2026-06-28) disagrees with the code: it calls "standard" the default, calls "minimal" a no-op and lists 49 filters. In code, minimal still filters, dedups and caps at 180 lines / 12000 chars, and there are 55 filters.

**Server settings:** /api/settings/compression keys enabled, defaultMode, exclusions, engines.rtk.{enabled,level}, rtkConfig.*, stackedPipeline, activeComboId, comboOverrides and enginesExplicit (true once an engines row is stored: src/lib/db/compression.ts L887).

**Other server paths:**

**Per request:** header x-omniroute-compression = off | default | engine:rtk (requires engines.rtk.enabled) | <combo name/id>. This header is itself the lossy opt-in.

feature: Compression engine codex-responses ("Responses Tool Output", PR #8010): conservative compression of Responses tool outputs
what_it_does:
An opt-in engine for tool outputs in Responses input[] (stackPriority 12, stackable). bodyAdapter maps each tool-output item to a role:tool message and tags whether it is eligible:
- local_shell_call_output and apply_patch_call_output are always eligible.
- function_call_output is eligible only when the function_call with the same call_id in the same request has a name that is not protected. Protected names: Read, Glob, Grep, Write, Edit, WebSearch, WebFetch, web_search, web_fetch, anything in preserveToolNames, and headless_retrieval.
- custom_tool_call_output is never eligible.

A string output is a candidate when it is at least minBytes (512) and at most maxCandidateBytes (512 KiB) and maxOutputBytes (2 MiB). Four rewrites are tried:
- JSON minify (lossless).
- compactDiff: keeps +/-/@@ lines plus up to 2 context lines after each change, and applies only if the result is at most maxLines×4 lines. No omission marker.
- compactSearch: when there are at least 8 path:line matches, keeps up to 3 match lines per path and drops every other line. No omission marker.
- collapseLines: applies to outputs of at least 24 lines that contain an error/warn/failed/exception/exit-code or 'x:1'/'f(1' line, or the words build/test/npm/make/cargo anywhere. It keeps the first 8 lines, the last 8 lines and 2 lines either side of each hit, capped at 160 kept lines, and inserts '[compressed log output: omitted N lines]'.

The smallest candidate is kept only if both bytes and codex tokens go down. A local_shell_call_output is skipped whenever any lossy candidate exists. Every eligible item in the whole input is processed again on every request: there is no age gate and no freeze.
defaults:
- Engine: off. DEFAULT_CODEX_RESPONSES_CONFIG is enabled=false, minBytes 512, maxOutputBytes 2097152, maxCandidateBytes 524288, maxLines 160, minSearchMatches 8, minLogLines 24, and preserveToolNames = the 7 Claude-Code tool names plus 7 lowercase variants.
- Master compression: off by default (enabled=false, defaultMode 'off'), and liveZone is off.
- Catalog: lossy:true, cacheImpact 'low'. lossyRequestPolicy puts codex-responses in LOSSY_SINGLE_MODES, so without an opt-in header any selection of it is downgraded to [session-dedup, lite].
- Selecting it as a mode or as a stacked step forces stepConfig.enabled=true.
controls:
- Settings API (/api/settings/compression; Dashboard Context & Cache > Compression):
  - enabled: the master switch; a header cannot turn it on.
  - exclusions: provider/model globs that force enabled=false.
  - engines['codex-responses'].enabled: required for the header engine:codex-responses. Saving the engines map sets enginesExplicit=true.
  - codexResponsesConfig.{minBytes, maxOutputBytes, maxCandidateBytes, maxLines, minSearchMatches, minLogLines, preserveToolNames}: global.
  - Also: comboOverrides, activeComboId, liveZone.enabled.
- Named compression combos (/api/context/combos) can carry the step {engine:'codex-responses'}.
- Request header x-omniroute-compression accepts engine:codex-responses, a combo name, or allow-lossy. The chosen plan is echoed in the X-OmniRoute-Compression response header.
- Client side: Codex [model_providers.<id>].http_headers / env_http_headers (rust-v0.157.1).
applies_to:
- **CX: yes, and only CX.** Codex 0.157.1 sends exec_command/shell_command/write_stdin results as function_call_output text, and those tool names are not protected, so they are eligible. apply_patch is a Freeform tool, so its output is custom_tool_call_output and never eligible.
- **FW: N/A.** A chat-completions messages[] body is not adapted, so it carries no eligibility tag and the engine returns it unchanged.
- **SEARCH: N/A.** It has no tool-output items.
quality_risk:
High for GPT-6 CX workers at max effort.
- **Unprotected tools:** the default protected names are Claude-Code tool names. Codex's own exec tools and its MCP function tools are unprotected.
- **Guard misses Codex:** upstream's local-shell lossy guard only matches local_shell_call_output, which Codex 0.157.1 never sends (0 occurrences in the binary's strings). File reads, rg searches and git diffs done through exec_command therefore get lossy rewrites.
- **Probe result:** I ran the unchanged pinned engine offline on synthetic Codex-shaped exec_command outputs:
  - rg -n: 17→8 lines, 6 of 12 matches dropped, exit-code line dropped, no marker.
  - A 120-line file read containing the word 'test' once: 125→17 lines, one marker.
  - git diff: 24→11 lines, context before the change and the exit-code line dropped, no marker.
  - The same rg output sent as local_shell_call_output: left raw.
- **Consequences:** grep hits and diff context go missing silently (apply_patch needs exact context), and the model may spend extra turns re-reading.
- **Second truncation:** Codex already truncates tool output itself with an explicit notice. This engine truncates again, silently, and Codex does not know about it.
- **Not the best CX candidate:** Codex's tool_output_token_limit is a client-native, per-profile lever.
cache_effect:
- **Not new-items-only:** apply() maps every message on every request.
- **Stable once warm:** the rewrite is a pure per-item function of the item text and the call name in the same request. With a constant config and the header sent on every request, the rewritten history only ever grows at the end, so prefix caching keeps hitting after warm-up.
- **Costs:**
  - Enabling it mid-session, or changing any codexResponsesConfig value or preserveToolNames, changes the prompt from the first rewritten item onward: one miss from that point for every live session.
  - Toggling the header per request flips the prefix back and forth.
- **liveZone is separate:** it is the upstream freeze-the-prefix, only-new-items mechanism. It is separate from this engine and live-disabled.
- **Default path unaffected:** with exclusions=['codex/*'] and master off, every CX request is skipped as 'excluded' and sent byte-identical.
token_effect:
- **Input side only:** the engine acts only on eligible tool outputs of at least 512 B. Output tokens are untouched; they are about 1.2% (117,065 vs 9,419,199 input in the brief's 122 rows).
- **Cache reuse:** about 94% of input is served from prompt cache.
  - Brief, 24h: 91,426,944 of 97,094,617 cached, so 5,667,673 (5.84%) uncached.
  - Snapshot /api/cache codex, cumulative, lastUpdated 2026-09-27T14:27:42Z: 110,864,768 of 118,355,678 cached (93.7%), so 7,490,910 uncached.
- **How savings arise:** a rewritten output is paid uncached once (already compressed) and afterwards read from cache at the smaller size.
- **Ceiling:** (share of eligible tool output in the roughly 6% uncached input) × (compression ratio). This is unmeasured: compression analytics has 0 engine rows because all 1600 skips were 'excluded'.
- **Offsets:** one cache miss per session at enable time, and extra re-read turns.
- **Net:** sign unknown, likely small.
proposed_config:
No PUT; keep the live values:
- /api/settings/compression: enabled=false, defaultMode='off', exclusions=['codex/*'], engines['codex-responses'].enabled=false (never save the engines map, because that sets enginesExplicit=true), codexResponsesConfig.enabled=false with upstream defaults, liveZone.enabled=false.
- Codex: no x-omniroute-compression in any [model_providers.*].http_headers or env_http_headers.

Why ON-OPT-IN is not reachable at this pin without touching another lane's default:
- Every route needs the master switch enabled and codex/* removed.
- engine:codex-responses needs engines['codex-responses'] on, which sets enginesExplicit. Every request without the header then derives codex-responses and is downgraded to [session-dedup, lite].
- A header naming a combo is shadowed by the default combo 'Standard Savings' while stackedPipeline is still the built-in one (source reading only).
- A routing-combo override needs a combo on CX plus allow-lossy.
- With master on and no exclusion, proactive context compaction (above 0.7 of the window) switches on for FW chat traffic to the same codex models.
- Exclusions match only provider/model, so they cannot split CX from FW. The gateway is keyless, so the per-key opt-out is unavailable, and it would not stop the reactive passes anyway.
- Recorded for a future overturn, not applied: preserveToolNames += exec_command, shell_command, write_stdin; a separate Codex provider block and profile with http_headers={"x-omniroute-compression"="engine:codex-responses"}.

feature: Compression master switch (enabled), defaultMode, autoTriggerTokens/autoTriggerMode, cacheMinutes, activeComboId/compressionComboId, and the default context combo 'Standard Savings' (id default-caveman)
what_it_does:
Per HTTP request (chatCore):
(1) Exclusions are checked first against the bare model and provider/model (live value codex/*). On a match, config.enabled is forced false and reactive compaction is off. A skip row with reason 'excluded' is written even while the master switch is off, and the body passes byte-identical.
(2) Otherwise enabled=false is a hard kill: no header can turn compression on.
(3) When enabled, precedence runs in this order: x-omniroute-compression header > routing-combo override or assigned compression combo > activeComboId (only if the id exists among the named combos) > auto-trigger > derived default.
- Auto-trigger fires when autoTriggerTokens>0 and the estimate is >= N, and uses autoTriggerMode. It is skipped when contextBudget.mode is floor or replace-autotrigger.
- The derived default comes from the engines map when enginesExplicit is true, otherwise from the legacy defaultMode.
- Header-less plans then get the lossy downgrade: lossy steps become session-dedup+lite.
- A cache-aware step follows. For codex it maps aggressive/ultra to standard and keeps the system prompt.

Case A: enabled=true, defaultMode=off, activeComboId=null, autoTrigger 0, enginesExplicit=false, no header.
- The plan is off (source=off). No engine runs, and no analytics row is written for non-excluded requests. The response header reads 'X-OmniRoute-Compression: off; source=off'.
- 'Standard Savings' is not applied. The legacy default-combo fallback needs a resolved 'stacked' mode plus the built-in rtk+caveman stackedPipeline.
- The master switch still arms reactive compaction for requests that are neither excluded nor native passthrough. It fires proactively when the estimate exceeds floor(0.7×(ctxLimit−toolTokens)), and as a last resort at or above the limit. It trims tool messages to 2000 chars, prunes images and purifies history.
- The master switch also defers combo overflow rejection.

Case B: activeComboId=default-caveman. Every header-less, non-excluded request runs stacked [session-dedup, lite] (source=active-profile).

Other controls:
- autoTriggerTokens=0 means disabled; the trigger requires a value strictly >0.
- cacheMinutes is only the liveZone memo TTL (clamped 1-60). It is inert while liveZone is off. It has nothing to do with the provider prompt cache or the semantic cache.
- The Codex Responses WebSocket bridge checks only `enabled`. It ignores exclusions, passes an empty combos map (so activeComboId cannot resolve) and passes a null header.

Effect of the master switch alone: under codex/* it changes no CX or FW body. Without that exclusion, CX over HTTP stays identical (plan off; reactive compaction skipped for native passthrough). FW changes only above the reactive threshold.

feature: Compression engine 'relevance': extractive sentence scoring against the last user query
what_it_does: A lossy engine that can run in a stacked pipeline or as a single mode (stackPriority 18). The query is the whole text of the LAST role:user message. Every role:user message is rewritten when its content is a string or exactly one text block. That includes the query message itself and every earlier user turn. System, assistant and tool messages are left alone. Each message is split on (?<=[.!?]\s). A sentence scores Jaccard(ASCII [a-z0-9] tokens, query tokens) minus boilerplateWeight times its boilerplate share. Sentences with digits, URLs, paths, k=v, code fences or error prefixes are always kept. The rest are admitted by score, if score >= overlapThreshold, until budgetPercent of the characters is used. If nothing survives, the top sentence is kept. Survivors are rejoined in their original order. The engine does not use the #13523 instruction-envelope preservation. Identical input gives identical output, but the output changes whenever the last user message changes.
defaults:
- The engine is off: schema enabled=false.
- Resolved defaults: overlapThreshold 0.1, budgetPercent 0.5, boilerplateWeight 0.5.
- apply() never reads `enabled`, so naming the engine in a pipeline runs it.
- It is not in DEFAULT_LADDER. It gets ladder rank 45 and factor 0.75 only through ladderOverride.
- The #14529 lossy policy removes it from any plan that a request header did not opt into.
- settings.relevanceConfig is declared (types.ts L248) but never read. Tuning works only through step.config in a combo pipeline.
applies_to:
- **CX: N/A.** Excluded by `codex/*`, and the master switch is off. All 1600 compression analytics rows are skip reason 'excluded'. If it ever became reachable: Codex 0.157.1 sends AGENTS.md as a role:user item, and the Responses adapter keeps it as role user, so the engine would prune it (probe G).
- **FW: N/A as wired.** GPT-6 FW calls resolve to provider codex (alias cx), so `codex/*` excludes them too. Reaching the engine would need the master switch on, an exclusion change and a named-combo header. It would harm S3 extraction and consolidation (probes C, J) and multi-step research runtimes, where the last user message is not the full intent (probes A, B).
- **SEARCH: N/A.** The search handlers and routes have no compression path (rg exit 1).
quality_risk:
High: the engine is lossy (catalog lossy:true). The query is the whole last user message. When that message carries the content (single-shot extraction, tool loops), the score reduces to |uniq(sentence)|/|uniq(message)|, which is a length ranking. After a short follow-up such as 'Continue.', nothing overlaps: only force-kept sentences plus one other survive.

Probes run on the pinned source, with only stats.ts stubbed:
- A, multi-turn agentic: the task message went 297->60 chars. Only its first sentence was kept; 'Never log card holder names or card numbers.' and 4 other constraints were dropped.
- B, tool loop: 3 of 6 constraints were dropped.

- J, JSON record: both instruction sentences, including 'Output strict JSON.', and 2 of 4 facts were dropped.
- G, Codex-style AGENTS.md user message: 4 rules became 1, the <INSTRUCTIONS> envelope was removed, and <\system-reminder> was cut short and left unclosed.
- H, real upstream doc as one message: 13 of 14 non-forced prose segments were dropped.
- I, the intended case (doc plus a separate question): 1 and 0 non-forced sentences were kept.

The ASCII-only tokenizer scores non-English sentences 0. Enabling it would degrade GPT-6 max-effort workers.
cache_effect:
It changes the prompt prefix, and the change depends on the query. Earlier user turns are rewritten against the newest user message, so the history bytes change at every new user turn. In probe D, the same history with two different follow-ups gave two different first-user texts, and neither matched the original. The prompt cache misses from the first rewritten user message onward. Within one tool loop the last user message stays the same, so the output is deterministic and the prefix is stable.

For Codex, the first rewritten item would be the AGENTS.md user message near the start of the input. Almost the whole prompt would then be billed as uncached on every user turn. cachingAware only protects the system prompt and downgrades aggressive/ultra; it does not guard relevance. The catalog rates cacheImpact 'moderate'. Against the live 93.7% cached share, this turns cached input into uncached input.
token_effect:
- **Live:** 0. It never runs (0 tokens saved, 1600 of 1600 rows skipped as 'excluded').
- **Potential:** only role:user text is touched, not tool outputs, assistant turns or the system message. It removes about 50% of those characters when enough sentences pass the threshold, and much more when they do not (probe A 297->60 chars, probe J 222->121).
- **Output:** unaffected. Output is about 1.2% of tokens in the call-log sample (117,065 of 9,536,264).
- **Net on these lanes:** small savings on user text, paid for with lost content, plus a cache break on every user turn that re-bills the history as uncached. No measured benefit.

feature: OmniGlyph compression engine: context rendered as images, measured only for Claude Fable 5 on a direct Anthropic route. omniglyph npm 1.4.0, preview (stable:false).
what_it_does:
Async-only lossy engine. It renders the system prompt, tool docs, old history and large tool outputs into 1-bit PNG pages and splices the image blocks back into the provider body. On the Claude wire it runs before translation; on OpenAI Chat/Responses it runs after translation. A profitability gate based on image-token billing math decides whether to convert. The adapter checks its gates in this order (all fail-closed, and any error becomes a skip):
1. supportsVision must be true (L133).
2. The provider transport must be 'direct' (L134). resolveOmniGlyphTransport treats only the 'anthropic' and 'claude' providers as direct.
3. Image fidelity must be 'byte-preserving' (L138-148).
4. Wire and stage checks (L150-185).
5. Profile resolution; a passthrough profile skips (L186-194).
6. The model must be inside the hard-coded coding-safe ceiling (L50) AND inside the chosen scope (L195-197). The package's allowed model bases are claude-fable-5 and gpt-5.6.
7. preserveSystemPrompt=true on a non-Claude wire skips with system_preservation_unsupported_on_wire (L198-210).
8. isModelImageable (L213).
Selection: the engine runs as single mode 'omniglyph' or as a stacked step. The catalog marks it lossy:true, so unless the request opts in it is downgraded to session-dedup+lite.
defaults:
- Compression defaults: enabled=false, defaultMode 'off', preserveSystemPrompt=true with mode 'always', every engine {enabled:false} (types.ts L421-436).
- omniglyph.profile defaults to 'aggressive' (types.ts L506-508, adapter L61).
- The engine is preview (adapter L291).
- Package default model bases are ['claude-fable-5','gpt-5.6']. OmniRoute pins the coding-safe ceiling, so environment settings can only narrow this list.
- The catalog lists it as lossy:true with cacheImpact 'high'.

feature: Compression engine: LLMLingua-2 semantic pruning (ONNX via @atjsh/llmlingua-2 + transformers.js), including ultra mode's SLM tier
what_it_does: Async stacked engine (stackPriority 35, not single-mode). It sends the prose of every non-system message to a token classifier and keeps about compressionRate of the tokens. That covers user, developer, assistant and tool messages; Responses input[] is mapped through bodyAdapter, and tool outputs become role 'tool'. Shielded and re-stitched verbatim: fenced and inline code, URLs, paths, identifiers, headings, tables, <\system-reminder>/<instructions>/<project-instructions> regions, XML tags and negations/absolutes. The model is uncased, so casing is restored heuristically. On any error or timeout it returns the original text. It also backs ultra mode's SLM tier (ultraEngine=slm or ultra.modelPath).
defaults: DEFAULT_COMPRESSION_CONFIG: enabled=false, defaultMode=off, every engine enabled=false, ultraEngine=heuristic, ultraSlmPrewarm=false, exclusions empty (types.ts L421-443, exclusions.ts L58). Step defaults: model=tinybert (atjsh/llmlingua-2-js-tinybert-meetingbank, 57 MB, fp32; bert-base 710 MB optional), minTokens=2000, compressionRate=0.5 (the keep ratio), modelPath='' so the model is lazily downloaded from the HF Hub into ${DATA_DIR}/models/llmlingua. Worker: CPU only; first call gets 60 s, warm calls 5 s per segment; idle eviction after 300 s; one process-wide FIFO queue.

- PUT /api/settings/compression: enabled (master switch; a header cannot turn it on); exclusions (glob on model or provider/model; forces enabled=false and a byte-identical body); engines.llmlingua.enabled (required for the header form engine:llmlingua); enginesExplicit; stackedPipeline / activeComboId; ultraEngine=slm; ultraSlmPrewarm; ultra.{modelPath, compressionRate, slmFallbackToAggressive}.

cache_effect:
Upstream rates it cacheImpact 'high' and excludes it from result memoization as 'model-backed/non-deterministic'.
- System messages and instructions are untouched, but the full history is re-run and rewritten on every turn.
- The minTokens=2000 floor covers all non-system text, so the turn that crosses it rewrites every earlier message: one full-prefix miss.
- Per-segment fail-open (5 s warm timeout, serialized process-wide queue, 300 s eviction) makes the output depend on load. The first segment that differs invalidates the cached suffix.
- The #3955 guard for caching providers (codex listed) downgrades only aggressive and ultra modes; a stacked llmlingua step passes through unguarded.
- FW one-shot calls keep their cached system prefix, so the savings there come only from deleting the document being extracted.
token_effect:

- Runtime cost: CPU fp32 inference, sequential per-segment awaits, re-run over the full history each turn, a single worker thread shared by every request.

feature: Output styles (terse-prose, less-code, ponytail, i-have-adhd, terse-cjk) and legacy caveman output mode
what_it_does:
The gateway injects a response-shaping instruction into the request prompt. It never rewrites the model's reply. applyOutputStyles resolves the selected styles in catalog order and joins their static text, fixed per (id, level, language). It appends SHARED_BOUNDARIES once and adds the idempotency marker "[OmniRoute Output Styles]".

Where the block lands:
- Responses body with no messages: appended as "\n\n" + block to the end of instructions after .trim(); if the body has input but no instructions, the block becomes instructions.
- Chat body: appended to the leading string system message; otherwise to the top-level system field; otherwise to a later string system message; otherwise added as a trailing system message.
- For FW calls to the codex provider, toResponses hoists the first system message into Responses instructions, so the block ends up at the top of the upstream prompt.

On chat bodies a keyword check over the last 3 messages skips the whole turn unless autoClarity is false. Legacy cavemanOutputMode {enabled, intensity} maps to [{terse-prose, intensity}] only when outputStyles is empty. The instruction text is identical to terse-prose, but the marker differs ("[OmniRoute Caveman Output Mode]"; observed).

quality_risk:
High for GPT-6 max-effort workers and structured lanes. The text steers persona and format; it is not lossless.
- terse-prose full: "Respond terse like smart caveman... Fragments OK", plus "Active every response until user asks for normal mode".

cache_effect:
What keeps the cache stable:
- The text is static per (id, level, language), so the prefix is stable while the gate stays constant.

What breaks it:
1. The block sits at the top of the prompt (instructions or first system message; toResponses L120-137). Turning it on, or changing a style, level or language, forces every session to re-pay the prefix. #13938 warns of the same one-time invalidation.
2. The gate changes per turn. With the live autoClarity=true, the chat-path keyword check flips injection turn by turn (observed on the pinned function):
   - "delete" -> irreversible_action
   - "security review" -> security_warning
   - "step by step" -> clarification_requested
   - "first run tests then deploy" -> order_sensitive_sequence
   The instructions prefix alternates, and each flip loses the conversation's cached prefix (the ~94% cached share).
3. .trim() rewrites the client's instructions and system bytes (apply.ts L150; outputMode.ts L233, L237, L251). Observed: the output no longer starts with the original bytes.
4. With autoDetect on, the language, and so the text, could vary per user message. It is off live.

The README calls the feature "cache-safe"; that holds only for point 1 with a constant gate. codex.ts L223-228 claims instructions are outside the GPT-5 cache key; that claim is unverified.

The possible saving is capped by the output share.

Measured split (122 recent rows): output 117,065 of 9,536,264 total tokens = 1.23%, about 960 output and 77,206 input tokens per request. Even the documented caveman 65% average output saving (a doc claim, not observed here) would save at most about 0.8% of all tokens. It would save less if those output counts include reasoning tokens, which styles do not target (unverified).

Injected input tokens per request, estimated with o200k_base (installed gpt-tokenizer; GPT-6 tokenizer unknown):

| Style | lite | full | ultra |
|---|---|---|---|
| terse-prose | 82 | 116 | 114 |
| less-code | 66 | 104 | 90 |
| ponytail | 97 | 290 | 155 |
| i-have-adhd | 106 | 319 | 155 |

Break-even on raw tokens needs visible output cut by more than 12% (terse-prose full), 33% (i-have-adhd full) or 70% (all four at full).

The gateway cannot measure the saving: telemetry sets tokensBefore = tokensAfter = estimatedTokens and receives no outputTokens. Live run-telemetry shows totalRuns=0.

feature: Compression engine: aggressive (summarizes and progressively ages old turns, and truncates tool results)
what_it_does: Deterministic, in-process rewrite of messages[]. Responses input[] is adapted so that only message and *_call_output items are mapped; reasoning and function_call items pass through untouched. Step 1 truncates EVERY tool output with no recency window: code-like output over 25 lines becomes head 20 + tail 5, shell output keeps its last 50 lines, grep keeps the top 30, JSON over 2000 chars becomes first5/last2, and errors keep head 10 + tail 3. Step 2 ages each message by its distance from the end, using the defaults verbatim=2, light=2, moderate=3, fullSummary=5. At distance <=2 a message stays verbatim. At distance 3 it only gets a '[COMPRESSED:aging:moderate]' tag, because caveman is called without options and is therefore disabled. At distance >=4 an assistant message becomes '[COMPRESSED:summary] Intents/Files/Errors/Last decision:<=200 chars' and a user message becomes its first line, up to 120 chars. Pure JSON is kept, and tool and developer roles are left alone by aging. Step 3 rule-summarizes any non-system message other than the last user message that is still over 8192 chars. If total savings are under 5%, caveman and then lite fallbacks run. Only role 'system' and the last user message are spared. WHO SUMMARIZES: a hard-coded RuleBasedSummarizer made of regex and heuristics. It uses no model, makes no extra calls and costs no tokens. The Summarizer interface is marked 'LLM-ready' but nothing is wired to it, and the separate `llm` engine ships a no-op backend.
defaults: Upstream pin: compression master enabled=false, defaultMode 'off', and every engine disabled, aggressive included (types.ts L421-443). DEFAULT_AGGRESSIVE_CONFIG: thresholds {fullSummary 5, moderate 3, light 2, verbatim 2}, all 5 toolStrategies true, summarizerEnabled true, maxTokensPerMessage 2048, minSavingsThreshold 0.05 (L553-565). The fullSummary threshold is never read, and the light tier cannot be reached at the defaults. Lossy request policy: aggressive set at operator level (defaultMode, engines, comboOverrides, active profile or auto-trigger) is silently downgraded to [session-dedup, lite] unless the request itself opts in through the x-omniroute-compression header. Cache guard: on a caching provider (openai/codex/azure/claude/...), single-mode aggressive becomes 'standard' with skipSystemPrompt=true and deterministicOnly=true, and deterministicOnly has no consumer at the pin. The adaptive contextBudget ladder includes aggressive; it runs after the lossy policy and emits a stacked plan.
controls: PUT /api/settings/compression keys: enabled (a hard kill; a header cannot turn compression on), defaultMode='aggressive', engines.aggressive.enabled, aggressive.{thresholds,toolStrategies,summarizerEnabled,maxTokensPerMessage,minSavingsThreshold}, autoTriggerMode/autoTriggerTokens, comboOverrides, activeComboId, contextBudget.mode floor|replace-autotrigger (+ladderOverride), ultra.slmFallbackToAggressive, exclusions, preserveSystemPromptMode. Compression combos (/api/context/combos) can contain the pipeline step {engine:'aggressive'}. A routing combo can set config.compressionMode or compressionOverride='aggressive' (chatCore L1573-1597). Request header x-omniroute-compression accepts: engine:aggressive (needs engines.aggressive.enabled), <compression combo name or id>, allow-lossy (keeps the operator plan), or off (headers.ts L41-46; planResolution L24-58). A per-API-key compressionEnabled=false turns it off for that key. Other surfaces: dashboard /dashboard/context/aggressive and CLI bin/cli/commands/compression.mjs.
applies_to: CX: does not run today. The live 'codex/*' exclusion sets config.enabled=false before the header is read, so the body passes through byte-identical. Codex is also a caching provider, so single-mode aggressive would become standard anyway; only a stacked combo or the adaptive ladder would run it, and those skip the guard. FW: cx/* chat-completions resolve to provider 'codex', and the live cache stats list only codex, so the same exclusion and downgrade apply. Single-shot extraction calls (system + one user message) would gain almost nothing because the system and last user message are spared, while multi-turn research runtimes would lose history. SEARCH: N/A. The /v1/search route (pin) and the /v1/alpha/search route (local build) reference neither chatCore nor compression (rg -c exit 1).
quality_risk: HIGH, from reading source at the pin (not executed). (1) The newest tool output is truncated too, so an agent sees 25 lines of a file it just read. (2) Earlier user turns, which carry task statements and injected instruction messages, are cut to a first line of at most 120 chars. Assistant turns are cut to a 200-char 'Last decision'. (3) Only role 'system' is protected; Responses 'developer' items are not. Step 3 summarizes any message over 8192 chars, recent ones included. (4) The instruction-block preservation from #13523 (extractPreservedBlocks) is used by caveman, ultra, llm and llmlingua, but aggressive.ts, progressiveAging.ts, summarizer.ts and toolResultCompressor.ts do not import it. (5) The docs promise 0-3 verbatim / 4-8 lite / 9-20 caveman / 20+ summary plus 'Context Window Awareness', but the code defaults do not implement that. (6) Codex interaction: the provider name 'OmniRoute' is not 'OpenAI', so RemoteCompactionSupport is Unsupported and Codex compacts locally with an ordinary /v1/responses turn that sends SUMMARIZATION_PROMPT. If aggressive ran, GPT-6 would write Codex's permanent handoff summary from already-aged history, and later turns would age Codex's own SUMMARY_PREFIX message (lossy on top of lossy). This conflicts with 'GPT-6 max-effort workers must not be degraded'.
cache_effect: Upstream rates cacheImpact 'high'. Tiers are counted from the end of the conversation, so every new turn re-renders the last ~4 messages (verbatim, then tag, then summary). The whole-request caveman/lite fallback can also flip when savings cross 5%. The cached prefix therefore breaks at the tier boundary each turn, and on the first aggressive request it breaks everywhere after the system prompt and instructions. Upstream's own guard (#3955, PR #4334) exists for this reason and downgrades aggressive to standard on codex. The stacked loops have no per-step guard, so the only way aggressive can run on codex also bypasses the cache protection. Live 24h prompt cache (codex only): 110,864,768 cached of 118,355,678 input tokens (93.7%). The net effect of aggressive has not been measured.
token_effect: Input side only, with zero extra model calls. Output, about 1% of tokens on the GPT-6 lanes, is untouched. Most of the removed tokens are history that is already served from cache at the cached rate, so the realizable saving is a fraction of upstream's claimed ~50%, which has not been measured here. The moderate tier's tag adds tokens. Live compression analytics: totalRequests 0, tokensSaved 0, skipped 1600 (all 'excluded'). No aggressive run has ever been recorded.
proposed_config: No write is needed; keep the live values: /api/settings/compression enabled=false, defaultMode='off', engines.aggressive.enabled=false, activeComboId=null, comboOverrides={}, autoTriggerTokens=0, autoTriggerMode not 'aggressive' (live 'lite'), contextBudget.mode='off', exclusions=['codex/*']. If adaptive mode is ever enabled, also set contextBudget.ladderOverride without 'aggressive' or 'ultra'. Keep default-caveman [session-dedup, lite] as the only compression combo and never add {engine:'aggressive'}. No routing combo may set compressionMode or compressionOverride='aggressive'. Lanes never send x-omniroute-compression engine:aggressive, allow-lossy, or a combo that contains aggressive. Then a paired A/B on one FW lane: control with no header vs x-omniroute-compression set to a combo containing [aggressive], same GPT-6 model and effort. feature: Compression engine `ultra` (Tier-A heuristic token pruning, optional Tier-B LLMLingua-2 SLM) and the 'Ultra tier' setting `ultraEngine` (Heuristic Tier-A default) with `ultraSlmPrewarm`
what_it_does:
Tier-A (pruneByScore). The prose of every non-system message is split on whitespace and scored. There is no size gate, because maxTokensPerMessage=0. Scores:
- 0.1 for stopwords: articles, pronouns, to/from/in/for/with, and/or/but, is/are/be.
- 0.2 for tokens of two characters or fewer, such as 'if'.
- 0.5-0.8 for other words.
- 1.0 for tokens containing a digit, '.', '_', '/', a URL, or a polarity/modal word (the #13454 fix).

Tokens scoring below minScoreThreshold (0.3) are dropped, up to (1-compressionRate)=50% of the words.

Before pruning, preservation.ts swaps these out and puts them back verbatim afterwards: fenced and inline code, URLs, CONST_CASE, versions, paths, headings, tables, and <\system-reminder>/<instructions> regions. Tier-A is deterministic and synchronous.

Tier-B (ultraEngine='slm'):
- Uses the same preservation, then sends prose to the LLMLingua-2 ONNX worker: TinyBERT-meetingbank on CPU at fp32, in 450-token segments.
- The worker handles one request at a time. It allows 60 s for the first call and 5 s after that, and is evicted after 300 s idle.
- On a timeout, error or no gain, that segment falls back to Tier-A and the run is tagged ultraTier=heuristic-fallback.
- Tier-B only runs when ultra is the single mode (applyUltraAsync). The `ultra` step in a stacked pipeline is always Tier-A.
- When ultra.modelPath is set, the llmlingua engine runs instead, and it falls back to `aggressive`.

Docs overstate the engine. The docs and engineCatalog claim ~75% savings, code-block thinning, binary-search truncation, all Aggressive features and always-on aging. The pinned code has none of these; applyAging is used only in aggressive.ts. ultra.enabled is read only by the UI, never by dispatch.
defaults:
Code defaults (types.ts L421-443, L600-606):
- compression.enabled=false, defaultMode='off'.
- ultraEngine='heuristic', ultraSlmPrewarm=false.
- ultra={enabled:false, compressionRate:0.5, minScoreThreshold:0.3, slmFallbackToAggressive:true, maxTokensPerMessage:0}, with no modelPath.
- engines.ultra.enabled=false.

The default SLM model is tinybert (57 MB). bert-base (710 MB) can only be selected through the llmlingua engine, because the ultra SLM path always passes model=undefined.

Lossy request policy: an ultra plan that the request did not ask for is replaced by session-dedup+lite.

Cache-aware guard: single-mode ultra becomes 'standard' on caching providers (codex, openai, azure, claude and others).
controls:
- **Settings (PUT /api/settings/compression):**
  - enabled: master switch; when off, a header cannot turn compression on.
  - ultraEngine ('heuristic'|'slm') and ultraSlmPrewarm (bool).
  - ultra{compressionRate 0-1, minScoreThreshold 0-1, slmFallbackToAggressive, modelPath, maxTokensPerMessage 0-32768, preserveSystemPrompt}, validated by the strict zod schema.
  - engines.ultra.enabled.
  - defaultMode or autoTriggerMode = 'ultra'.
  - comboOverrides, stackedPipeline step {engine:'ultra'}, exclusions, preserveSystemPromptMode.
- **Combos:**
  - Named compression combos (/api/context/combos).
  - Routing-combo config.compressionMode or compressionOverride = 'ultra'.
- **Request header X-OmniRoute-Compression:**
  - off | default.
  - engine:ultra, which requires engines.ultra.enabled.
  - <combo name or id>.
  - allow-lossy, which keeps the operator plan.
- **Other switches:**
  - A per-connection providerSpecificData.cache.supportsPromptCaching=false bypasses the caching guard.
  - A per-API-key compressionEnabled=false turns compression off for that key.
- **Dashboard:** 'Ultra tier' select and 'Pre-warm SLM model on enable' toggle.
- **Optional dependencies:** @atjsh/llmlingua-2, @huggingface/transformers, js-tiktoken, onnxruntime-node.
- **Model cache:** ${DATA_DIR}/models/llmlingua, downloaded from the HF Hub unless modelPath is set.
applies_to:
- **CX: N/A.** All traffic is codex/* (24h cache-health: 1486 calls, all codex/gpt-6-*). exclusions=['codex/*'] skips the whole compression pipeline and leaves the body byte-identical. Even without that exclusion, codex is a caching provider, so single-mode ultra would be rewritten to 'standard'.
- **FW: N/A today.** GPT-6 FW calls go to the same codex provider, so they are excluded and cache-guarded too. Ultra would only become reachable through a non-caching provider connection, or through a stacked combo containing ultra after lifting the exclusion.
- **SEARCH: N/A.** The /v1/search and /v1/alpha/search routes contain no compression calls.

Structure defect (observed): pruneByScore trims each prose part and the parts are rejoined with '', so prose runs into the next fence ('Carol.```json'). The fence no longer starts a line, which contradicts the 'never mangles structured content' claim in ultra.ts. Trailing whitespace also changes which words are pruned.

Tier-B (inferred from code and upstream issue #13455, not reproduced here):
- ultraEntry calls workerBackend directly. That skips the llmlingua engine's negation/tag shielding and case restoration (the #13768 fixes).
- So the #13455 defects stay on this path: lower-cased output, dropped negations, broken tags.
- The ultra.ts L216-218 comment that says otherwise is wrong.
- Tier-B adds serialized CPU inference latency, up to 5 s per segment warm and 60 s on the first call.
- It downloads an unpinned model from the HF Hub at runtime.

**Negative.**

Upstream's own view:

- It excludes ultra from the result memo as non-deterministic.

Tier-A:
- Tier-A is deterministic (observed: two identical calls gave byte-equal output), so a steady session re-caches the pruned prefix.

Tier-B:
- Tier-B falls back per segment on timeout, so its output can differ between requests. That would cause recurring prefix misses.

Guard gap:
- The downgrade applies to the plan's mode only.
- A stacked plan containing {engine:'ultra'} passes through unchanged on caching providers.
- deterministicOnly is computed but never read.

overturn_condition:
All of the following must hold:
1. A lane measurably hits context-limit failures on a non-caching provider or a local model.
2. That lane's own A/B, against off and against lossless engines (session-dedup, ccr, headroom, rtk), shows:
   - task quality not degraded (extraction F1, relation direction, json_schema validity);
   - cache-read share not reduced.
3. Upstream fixes the trim/fence-glue defect, or the lane's payloads are shown to be unaffected by it.
4. For Tier-B:
   - the ultraEntry path gets guards equivalent to #13768 (or is routed through the llmlingua engine);
   - the model is pinned offline through modelPath.
5. The stacked cache-guard gap is closed, or the lane is non-caching.
